title: The human body
description: How the body's main systems work, with the everyday numbers worth knowing.

ideas.title: Heart and blood
ideas.summary: The heart pumps blood round two loops, first to the lungs for oxygen and then out to the rest of the body.

items.q: How many chambers does the human heart have, and what are they called?
items.a: Four: two atria and two ventricles

items.q: Which chamber of the human heart pumps oxygen-rich blood out to the body?
Which kind of blood vessel carries blood away from the heart?
Which protein in red blood cells carries oxygen?
What is the normal range for an adult's resting heart rate?

ideas.title: Breathing and gas exchange
ideas.summary: The lungs take in oxygen and give up carbon dioxide across millions of tiny, thin-walled air sacs.

items.q: What are the tiny air sacs in the lungs called, where oxygen passes into the blood?
Which dome-shaped muscle beneath the lungs does most of the work of breathing?
Which tube carries air from the throat down toward the lungs?

ideas.title: Food, fuel and waste
ideas.summary: The gut absorbs nutrients, the liver and pancreas manage them, and the kidneys clear waste from the blood.

items.q: In which part of the human digestive tract are most nutrients absorbed?
Which hormone, made by the pancreas, lowers the level of sugar in the blood?
Which organ of the human body makes bile?
What is the main job of the kidneys?
items.a: They filter the blood, removing waste and excess water as urine

ideas.title: Nerves and the brain
ideas.summary: Nerve cells carry fast electrical signals, and the brain and spinal cord turn them into sensing and action.

items.q: Which two structures make up the human central nervous system?
items.a: The brain and the spinal cord

items.q: What is the junction called where one nerve cell passes a signal to the next?
Which part of the human brain coordinates balance and fine movement?
Roughly how many neurons does the human brain contain?

ideas.title: Bones and muscles
ideas.summary: Bones give the body its frame, and muscles move it by pulling on them across joints.

items.q: How many bones does an adult human have?
What is the longest bone in the human body?
In the human body, what kind of tissue connects a muscle to a bone?
In the human body, what kind of tissue connects one bone to another at a joint?

ideas.title: Defense and balance
ideas.summary: The body holds its inner conditions steady, and its immune system learns to recognize what does not belong.

items.q: What is normal human body temperature?
In physiology, what is homeostasis?
items.a: Keeping the body's internal conditions stable as conditions outside change

items.q: In the immune system, what do antibodies do?
items.a: They bind to specific foreign molecules, marking invaders for destruction

items.q: How does a vaccine protect a person against a disease?
items.a: It trains the immune system to recognize the germ without causing the illness
